# [CS085] NoSQL Injection (nosql-injection)

Database-side code is built from untrusted data: a Redis Lua script or MongoDB $where, $function or $accumulator JavaScript.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Severity** | HIGH |
| **Category** | Security |
| **CWE** | [CWE-943](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/943.html) |
| **OWASP** | A05:2025 |
| **Auto-Fix supported** | No |

## Why It Matters in Go

Redis EVAL and MongoDB $where run the given text as code on the database server, so input concatenated into it can read or change any key or document the connection can reach. The taint engine follows request data to go-redis Eval, EvalRO, ScriptLoad and NewScript across functions; MongoDB query documents (bson.M, bson.D or a map) are checked within the function that builds them. Ordinary filter values such as bson.M{"name": name} are not reported: the driver sends them as data.

## Vulnerable / Problematic Example

```go
func count(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	field := r.FormValue("field")
	rdb.Eval(r.Context(), "return redis.call('HGET', KEYS[1], '"+field+"')", []string{"stats"})
	coll.Find(r.Context(), bson.M{"$where": "this.owner == '" + r.FormValue("owner") + "'"})
}
```

## Safe / Idiomatic Go Pattern

```go
var hget = redis.NewScript("return redis.call('HGET', KEYS[1], ARGV[1])")

func count(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	hget.Run(r.Context(), rdb, []string{"stats"}, r.FormValue("field"))
	coll.Find(r.Context(), bson.M{"owner": r.FormValue("owner")})
}
```

## Configuration & Suppression

Disable the rule for the whole module in `.codexsentinel.yaml`:

```yaml
rules:
  disabled: [nosql-injection]
```

Change its severity:

```yaml
rules:
  severity_overrides:
    nosql-injection: low
```

Suppress one reviewed finding on its line, with the reason:

```go
//codex:ignore nosql-injection -- <reason>
```

Or ignore it under a path in `.codexsentinel.ignore`:

```text
internal/legacy/** nosql-injection
```
